uncited: The Slab/Min-Max method determines if a ray intersects an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) by computing the entry ($t_{near}$) and exit ($t_{far}$) distances along the ray parameter $t$.
It treats the box as the intersection of three pairs of parallel planes (slabs) [Parent].

It sets itself apart from [Ray-box intersection](776-ray-box-intersection.md) by explicitly providing the scalar interval $[t_{min}, t_{max}]$ required for subsequent volume sampling or traversal, rather than just a boolean hit test.
The method relies on the parametric ray equation $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$, where $\mathbf{o}$ is the origin and $\mathbf{d}$ is the direction.
An AABB is defined by $\mathbf{min} = (x_{min}, y_{min}, z_{min})$ and $\mathbf{max} = (x_{max}, y_{max}, z_{max})$.
A ray intersects the box if $t_{min} \le t_{max}$ and $t_{max} \ge 0$ (for forward rays) [S2, unofficial].
The slab method is a standard primitive intersection test in computer graphics.
